previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of aortic stenosis, chronic hyponatremia due to SIADH, atrial fibrillation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted from an extended care facility for hypotension, chest pain, and rapid atrial fibrillation. Initial management included IV fluids and metoprolol for rate control, but his heart rate remained elevated. Digoxin was initiated at a low dose after a brief pause due to hypotension, leading to improved rate control. Valsartan was held throughout admission due to low blood pressure. His pulmonary congestion resolved, and labs showed stable sodium and no evidence of myocardial injury. He was discharged back to extended care on digoxin, increased metoprolol, and continued home medications for bronchitis and pain, with follow-up arranged for digoxin level monitoring and cardiology evaluation.
